newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nemtsov offers Japan investors home phone number.
newsitem.headline: Nemtsov offers Japan investors home phone number.

text.p: Boris Nemtsov, Russia's reform-minded first deputy prime minister, offered Japanese business interests his personal support for new investment in Russia on Tuesday, even if it meant calling him at his home. "If you can't reach me at my administrative offices, reach me on my mobile phone," Nemtsov told an elite gathering of Japan's business community.
"If you can't reach me on my mobile phone, reach me at home," he added.

Nemtsov, whose comments were delivered at a speech organised by the powerful Japanese business lobby, Keidanren, is part of an 80-strong Russian delegation visiting Japan for three days in order to foster greater economic ties between the two countries.
Nemtsov, 38, came to Tokyo promising a broad package of reforms aimed at clearing the way for new and existing Japanese investments in Russia.
Japanese industry sources have said their investments in Russia have been hampered by funding problems and red tape.

But Nemtsov has promised to help individual business interests as they combat Russia's often slow-moving bureaucracy, most recently promising completely tax-free conditions to Japanese oil companies operating in Russia's oil-rich Sakhalin Island region.
Nemtsov's action-minded methods have been praised by President Boris Yeltsin.

Speaking in Moscow on Monday, Yeltsin said his new team of Nemtsov and Anatoly Chubais, the other first deputy prime minister, had "positively affected the style, methods and results" of the government's work.
